confidence_notes: I checked food and drink prices with two web searches. Sources were crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregators (mylifeelsewhere, traveltables, last updated July 2023) and third-party guide listings of KES price ranges at venues in the Nyali tourist area. The aggregators disagree: cappuccino is about $2.3 on one and $3.2 on the other, and beer is about $1.9 on one and $2.7 on the other. I set the anchors near the middle and adjusted for inflation to mid-2026. The inexpensive meal is set above the very low local-eatery figure (about $2.3) to reflect the kind of simple sit-down restaurant a visitor would use. The mid-range meal for two is less certain. Traveltables gives about $45, which looks high next to its other prices, so I lowered it. For cocktails and wine I used venue price ranges (cocktails about KES 400-1,200, wine about KES 500-900 a glass) and checked them against the local price ratio to beer. These are tourist-area figures, so cheaper local bars will charge less. Accommodation is a model estimate from general knowledge only; I did not search booking sites. Mombasa has few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-hostel anchors are especially uncertain. Three-star prices change with the beach season (July is high season).
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink are based on aggregator data for Mombasa itself and venue price ranges in Nyali. Accommodation is reasoned from Mombasa's role as Kenya's main coastal tourist city. It is somewhat cheaper than Nairobi for basic lodging and comparable to Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar Town for budget and mid-range rooms.
